title: Client-supplied UserId/UserName copied verbatim into order and Buyer aggregates
owner_hint: no CODEOWNERS entry; top committer: Rob Conery / David Fowler; component: Ordering.API/
rationale: CreateOrderCommandHandler now derives UserId/UserName from the already-injected IIdentityService (GetUserIdentity/GetUserName) instead of message fields, with a fail-closed guard returning false when no sub claim is present. CreateOrderRequest keeps its DTO shape; the body fields are simply no longer consumed for attribution.
variants_checked: CreateOrderDraftCommandHandler never reads BuyerId (pure price draft, not persisted); ValidateOrAddBuyerAggregate and Basket.API handlers are downstream and now receive identity-derived values; IdentifiedCommandHandler UserId use is log-only.
bypass_considered: Attacker-supplied UserId/UserName (any casing/encoding) never reach the Order aggregate, OrderStartedDomainEvent, or integration event; unauthenticated requests are rejected by the new guard.
test_note: Handle_creates_order_for_identity_service_user_not_body_user in tests/Ordering.UnitTests/Application/NewOrderCommandHandlerTest.cs asserts the persisted events carry the identity-service id, not the body value.
review_reason: Fix sits exactly at the sink where body identity was consumed, sourced from the same trusted mechanism as the read path; fail-closed guard added; test-only second hunk uses existing helpers.
